definitions.short: a Chittite , or descendant of Cheth
definitions.full: H2850. Chitti חִתִּי adjective and name, of a people Hittite(s) (Egyptian –-tá, –etá W Max Müll Asien u. Europa, 319 ff. ; Assyrian –atti , Schr KG 192 ff. COT on Gen 10:19 Dl Pa, 269 ff. ; Tel el-Amarna –atti, –atta Bez Tel el Amarn. Brit. Mus. 150 ) — masculine always with article הַחִתִּי 23:10 ; Exod 3:8 +; feminine חִתִּית Ezek 16:3 , 45 ; masculine plural הַחִתִּים Josh 1:4 3 t.; feminine plural חִתִּיֹּת 1Kin 11:1 ; — 1. adjective , of seller of Machpelah to Abraham, הַחִתִּי עֶפְרוֺן Gen 23:10 ; 49:29-30 , 50:13 ; ׳הַח בֶּןצֹֿחַר עֶפְרֹן 25:9 (all P); of fathers of Esau's wives ׳הַח בְּאֵרִי 26:34 ; הַח ׳אֵילוֺן 26:34 ; 36:2 (all P); also of warriors of David, הַח ׳אֲחִימֶלֶךְ 1Sam 26:6 , and especially הַח ׳אוּרִיָּה 2Sam 11:3 , 6 , 17 , 21 , 24 ; 12:9-10 , 23:39 ; 1Kin 15:5 ; 1Chr 11:41 ; feminine singular = substantive, only of (religious) ancestry of Jerusalem Ezek 16:3 thy father was the Amorite, and thy mother was a Hittite woman חִתִּית , similarly 16:45 ; feminine plural = substantive of Solomon's foreign wives, חִתִּיֹּת 1Kin 11:1 Hittite women (+ צֵדְנִיֹּת אֲדֹמִיֹּת, עַמּוֺנִיּוֺת, מוֺאֲבִיּוֺת, ). 2. n. usually a. collective הַחִתִּי the Hittites: in lists of Canaanitish peoples Gen 15:20 (JE), Exod 3:8 , 11 (both J), 13:5 ; 23:23 , 28 ; 33:2 ; 34:11 ; Num 13:29 ; Josh 3:10 (all J E), Deut 7:1 ; 20:17 ; Josh 9:1 ; 12:8 ; 24:11 (all D); read also for הַחִוִּי Judg 3:3 (so We Mey Bu Urg 350 ); in Josh 11:3 (D) strike out הַחִתִּי We Mey Bu l.c. , and read then הַחִתִּי for הַחִוִּי v b (so ᵐ5 , not ᵐ5 L ); further 1Kin 9:20 2Chr 8:7 ; Ezra 9:1 ; Neh 9:8 . b. plural הַחִתִּים אֶרֶץ כֹּל ׃הַחִתִּים Josh 1:4 (D) nearly = land of Canaanites; הַח ׳ארץ specifically of northern home of Hittites Judg 1:26 ; so also 2Sam 24:6 where read קֵ֫דְשָׁה הַחִתִּים אֶרֶץ (for חָדְשִׁי תחתים ᵑ0 , see קֵדֶשׁ חָדְשִׁי, ); הַחִתִּים מַלְכֵי 1Kin 10:29 2Chr 1:17 (both + אֲרָם מַלְכֵי ), 2Kin 7:6 (+ מִצְרַיִם מַלְכֵי , both feared by אֲרָם ). Hence it appears that (םׅ הַחִתִּי had their proper seat in the north — where also they were encountered by Assyrians from time of Tiglath-Pileser I (see Schr Dl 1. c .), and by Egyptians from time of Tutmes III (see W Max Müll. l.c. ) — (compare also Judg 3:3 ; Josh 11:3 above), but that individual Hittites were known in Israel (compare, besides 1Sam 2:6 ; 2Sam 11:3 etc., 1Kin 9:20 above); that the Hittites were regarded (by J E D) as one of the peoples of Canaan, and that the name even came to be used in more General sense for Canaanites. Only in P do they appear as having a definite settlement in the south, and are designated by בְּנֵיחֵֿת (see חֵת ), as well as by the adjective הַחִתִּי .
